title: The Reeb triad as an internal $\mathrm{SU}(2)$, and what it is not
html:
Remark. The Reeb triad as an internal \mathrm{SU}(2), and what it is not

The bracket [M_i, M_j] = 2M_k is a theorem about the quaternions. Reading it as a physical symmetry is a separate step, and this remark keeps the two apart.

The reading is: the Reeb flow along the fibres of the Bring cone carries an internal \mathrm{SU}(2) structure on the localized states, so that the quaternionic spectral resolvents, which already take values in \mathrm{Im}\,\mathbb{H}, are sections of a bundle whose structure group is the one the triad generates. On the formal side this is the unit-quaternion picture: \mathrm{SU}(2) is \{q \in \mathbb{H} : |q|^2 = 1\}, acting on a quaternionic state \psi by \psi \mapsto g\psi on the left and \psi \mapsto \psi g on the right, and the two actions commute. A quaternion's four real degrees of freedom are two complex ones, so \psi is an \mathrm{SU}(2) doublet, and the \mathrm{U}(1) generated by a single imaginary unit sits inside that \mathrm{SU}(2) — the electroweak alignment.

Two limits are worth stating plainly.

First, the identification of the Reeb \mathrm{SU}(2) with a gauge symmetry of the physical theory is interpretive. The bracket forces the Lie algebra; it does not by itself say which field the algebra acts on.

Second, the triad is an \mathrm{SU}(2) and nothing larger. Its three Reeb fields are the three dimensions of \mathfrak{su}(2), the adjoint — not a three-dimensional fundamental representation. This layer is therefore not a source of colour, and reading the count "three" as evidence for \mathrm{SU}(3) would be an equivocation between the adjoint and the fundamental.

The first limit has a testable consequence, which is what keeps it from being a disclaimer. Morita's quaternionic formulation of the Weinberg–Salam theory [morita1982] builds fermions and Higgs mesons over \mathbb{H} and finds that what it reproduces is not the Standard Model gauge group but the left–right symmetric one, \mathrm{SU}(2)_L \times \mathrm{SU}(2)_R \times \mathrm{U}(1) — precisely because both the left and the right unit-quaternion actions are available and neither is distinguished by the algebra. The same is true of the Reeb triad here: the construction has no way to prefer g\psi over \psi g.

So if the Reeb \mathrm{SU}(2) is the electroweak \mathrm{SU}(2), the framework inherits a left–right symmetric gauge sector and owes an account of how the right-handed factor is broken — Morita correlates that breakdown with the existence of a Fock space for gauge singlets but not for quaternionic states. That consequence is checkable against the framework, so the identification is falsifiable and not only interpretive.
